hook.text: Romeo and Juliet. Tristan and Isolde. Layla and Majnun. Why does every culture have a tragic forbidden love story?

buildup.text: Cross-culturally, forbidden love stories reinforce social boundaries by showing the cost of breaking them.

discovery.text: The 'Romeo and Juliet effect': parental opposition increases romantic attraction. Forbidden things grow more desirable.

twist.text: The stories warn, but audiences read them as aspirations. Culture says 'don't'; the audience hears 'love conquers all.'

climax.text: Every generation rebels through love. Interracial, interfaith, same-sex—forbidden love slowly changes society's rules.

punchline.text: Forbidden love stories aren't about love. They're about power.

quiz.question: What is the 'Romeo and Juliet effect'?
